newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber up slightly after housing report.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber up slightly after housing report.

text.p: A better-than-expected U.S. housing starts report prompted abn early rise in CME lumber futures, traders said.

The housing report showed a 2.6 percent increase in April starts against expectations for a small decline. But bullishness was limited by the largest increase in starts coming in multi-family units, traders said.
Initial resistaince in futures was also cited following another decline in cash prices, they said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $382, off $2 from both midweek and week-ago levels.
At 0928 CDT, lumber stood $2.20 to $2.00 higher, with only July and September trading. July was up $2.20 at $394.00 and September up $2.00 at $283.80 per tbf.
